AI selloff hits India too: TD Power, HFCL, Sterlite, other power capex-linked stocks crash up to 15%
sum: TD Power and Thermax were among the worst-hit stocks, plunging 15% each during the session. HFCL and Sterlite Technologies, which have emerged as major AI beneficiaries in 2026, were locked in the 5% lower circuit. Hitachi Energy and CG Power fell 5% and 7%, respectively, while Aeroflex Industries and KRN Heat Exchanger declined 5% in morning trade.

The sell-off came amid fears that gains by the Democratic Party in the US midterm elections could lead to restrictions on data centre expansion and slow down the country's artificial intelligence infrastructure development.

Concerns over a possible slowdown in artificial intelligence-related investments wiped out around $2.5 trillion in US stock market value on Thursday, as a sharp sell-off in technology stocks erased Wall Street's post-election rally.

The technology-heavy Nasdaq Composite plunged 5.52% to close at 24,315, marking its steepest single-day decline since April 2025, when US President Donald Trump announced sweeping global tariffs. The sell-off pushed the index more than 10% below its record high hit last month, putting it in correction territory.

The sell-off across Asia's tech-heavy markets deepened on Friday, as concerns over tighter regulatory scrutiny and a potential slowdown in AI infrastructure spending triggered a sharp retreat in equities. The rout followed the steepest decline in US stocks since the tariff-induced 'Liberation Day' sell-off in April 2025.

Japan's Kioxia plunged 14%, while Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) fell as much as 8.5% in Taiwan. SoftBank Group, a major investor in AI, tumbled 11%, while the cost of insuring against a debt default by the Japanese conglomerate surged to its highest level in four years.

sum: Hitachi, Ltd. provides digital system and services, green energy and mobility, and connective industry solutions in Japan and internationally. It operates through Digital Systems & Services, Energy, Mobility, Connective Industries, and Others segments. The company offers system integration, consulting, cloud services, storage, servers, software, and ATMs; finance solutions, social infrastructure information systems, public IT solutions, industrial internet of things, digital engineering, control system, and cloud services; and IT products, such as data management and storage. It also provides energy power grids, clean, nuclear, renewable energy, transmission, distribution, digital service, service and consulting, and utility solutions; and railway systems, such as rolling stock, signaling, supervision, telecommunications, and ticketing and payment solutions; automotive automation, including automotive assembly, glass applications, press automation, powertrain, paint and sealer applications, and tyre and wheel systems; and e-mobility solutions, as well as elevators and escalators, home appliances, air conditioners, industry and distribution solution, water and environment solutions, and industrial machinery. Further, it provides automated manufacturing and robotic technologies, industrial & portable air compressors, industrial equipment systems, build-to-order industrial equipment, water environment solution, ATM and cash recycling. Hitachi, Ltd. was founded in 1910 and is headquartered in Tokyo, Japan.

Hitachi Energy India net profit surges 123.5% to ₹294.2 crore in Q1FY27
sum: Hitachi Energy India reported strong Q1FY27 results with net profit rising 123.5% YoY to ₹294.2 crore and revenue surging 68.6% to ₹2,493.7 crore. Order inflows stood at ₹5,096.5 crore with a record backlog of ₹32,222.1 crore, while a ₹2,000 crore manufacturing facility was initiated in Vadodara.
*this image is generated using AI for illustrative purposes only.

Hitachi Energy India Limited reported a net profit of ₹294.2 crore for the first quarter ended June 30, 2026 (Q1FY27), marking a 123.5% year-on-year increase from ₹131.6 crore in Q1FY26. Revenue from operations surged 68.6% YoY to ₹2,493.7 crore, driven by robust execution across power grids, data centers, and renewable energy segments. The company's operational EBITDA expanded 135% to ₹399.9 crore, with margins improving to 16.0% from 11.5% in the prior year period. This performance was underpinned by record order inflows and significant operational efficiencies.

The Board of Directors approved the unaudited financial results during its meeting on August 07, 2026. The results were reviewed by M/s. S. R. Batliboi & Associates LLP, the statutory auditors. The filing was submitted to the BSE and NSE pursuant to Regulation 30 of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015. Additionally, the Board approved amendments to the Code of Conduct for Prevention of Insider Trading as required under Regulation 8(2) of the SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015. The results were published in "The Hindu Business Line" and "Vijaya Karnataka" on August 08, 2026, in compliance with Regulation 47 of the SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015.

Order inflows totaled ₹5,096.5 crore in Q1FY27. Excluding high-voltage direct current (HVDC) projects, orders grew 26.1% YoY. The company secured a flagship 2 GW wind power evacuation order in Europe and its first battery energy storage system (BESS) project, a 165 MW / 330 MWh facility in Andhra Pradesh. In the domestic market, Hitachi Energy won a prestigious order for a 100 GW solar park in western India, including load pooling stations with 56 bays of 400 kV GIS. Data center orders included over 560 MVA power transformers and a significant 40x2500 KVA project in Hyderabad for a leading Indian multinational conglomerate.

items.t: Fujitsu shares slump 16% on weak first-half earnings
sum: Investing.com-- Fujitsu (TYO:6702) shares slumped 16% on Friday after the Japanese technology company reported weaker profit for the first half of fiscal 2026, as rising component costs and increased research and development spending weighed on earnings.

The company's adjusted operating profit fell 6.1% to 113.9 billion yen ($720 million) in the six months ended September, despite revenue rising 3.8% to 1.63 trillion yen, Fujitsu reported on Thursday.
Shares of the company fell 16.2% to 3,622.0 yen by 04:26 GMT.

Hardware Solutions profit dropped 64% to 4.5 billion yen as higher memory chip costs squeezed margins, while profit in its Ubiquitous Solutions business fell 38.3% amid a pullback in demand for Windows 10-related upgrades.
Increased investment in advanced technologies, including next-generation CPUs and quantum computing, also weighed on profitability.

Service Solutions, Fujitsu's core business, provided some support, with revenue rising 5.9% and adjusted operating profit increasing 11.8% to 133.7 billion yen, driven by demand for its Uvance digital transformation offerings.

Fujitsu maintained its full-year forecast for adjusted operating profit of 425 billion yen and revenue of 3.51 trillion yen, implying a stronger second-half performance will be needed to meet its earnings target.

Advantest shares jump as AI chip demand drives earnings outlook upgrade
sum: Investing.com-- Advantest Corp. (TYO:6857) shares jumped on Thursday after the semiconductor testing equipment maker raised its full-year earnings forecast, citing stronger-than-expected demand for equipment used to test artificial intelligence chips.
Advantest shares rose 7.3% to 3,7480 yen by 05:29 GMT, after climbing as much as 9.1% earlier in the session, helping lift Japan's Nikkei share average.

The company raised its operating profit forecast for the fiscal year ending March 2027 to 967 billion yen ($6.3 billion) from 846 billion yen, an increase of 14%, following a sharp rise in first-half earnings.
The company also lifted its full-year revenue forecast to 1.863 trillion yen from 1.714 trillion yen.
For the six months ended September, revenue rose 60.5% year-on-year to 845.2 billion yen, while operating profit surged 96.5% to 456.8 billion yen. Net profit climbed 116.8% to 368.1 billion yen.

Advantest said demand for testing high-performance AI semiconductors was expanding faster than expected as investment in data centres increased. It also expects the semiconductor tester market to reach a record high as demand for chips used in AI inference grows.

Industrials Stock Picks: Find out which stock is Elara Capital is betting on from the group
sum: Elara Capital initiated coverage on three industrials stocks: a buy for GE Vernova T&D India, an accumulate for Siemens Energy India, and a sell for Hitachi Energy India, citing strong growth driven by transmission opportunities, renewables, and data centers.
Brokerage firm Elara Capital initiated coverage on three industrial stocks, Ge Vernova T&D Ltd., Siemens Energy India Ltd., and Hitachi Energy India Ltd. on Wednesday, October 14.

It has initiated coverage with a "buy" recommendation on GE Vernova T&D India Ltd. with a target price of ₹5,547 per share (32% upside), an "accumulate" rating on Siemens Energy India Ltd. with a target price of ₹3,699 (18.4% upside) and a "sell" recommendation on Hitachi Energy India Ltd. with a target price of ₹29,190 per share (3.5% downside). GE Vernova T&D India is also Elara's top pick within the space.

Elara Capital in its note on industrials said the transmission and distribution (T&D) equipment sector is entering its mid-cycle, with data centres, battery energy storage system (BESS), renewables and electrification broadening demand beyond conventional transmission.

The note further added that India's ₹15 lakh crore transmission opportunity through the financial year 2026 and $606 billion global grid investment by the calendar year 2029 offer strong visibility for equipment manufacturers. Also, India's cost competitiveness and expanding extra high voltage (EHV) capability create a structural export opportunity.

Easing land/right of way (RoW) and project-readiness concerns with rising equipment capacity should support a recovery in transmission-based competitive bidding (TBCB) ordering and improve conversion from awarded projects into equipment orders and execution, Elara Capital said.

sum: Hitachi Construction Machinery Co.’s shares fell the most in almost three weeks after its major shareholder Hitachi Ltd. offloaded all holding, in the latest move by the Japanese conglomerate to divest some of its assets to focus on core businesses.

Hitachi will sell 10.09% stake in the machinery company, according to a release on Tuesday. That would be worth about ¥118 billion ($740 million) based on the Tuesday’s closing price at ¥5,490. SMBC Nikko Securities Inc. is the arranger of the share sale.

Hitachi has been cutting its stake in the machinery firm as part of its efforts to concentrate resources on core businesses including IT services and energy. The company sold about 8% of Hitachi Construction shares in block trades in May.

Hitachi and Toshiba to Deliver the Future of High-Speed Rolling Stock to Taiwan
sum: Tokyo and Kawasaki, Japan, July 30, 2026, Hitachi Toshiba Supreme Consortium (“HTSC”), a consortium consisting of Hitachi, Ltd. (TSE:6501, “Hitachi”), Toshiba Corporation (“Toshiba”) and others today announced that it has completed manufacturing the first batch of N700ST, the new high-speed railcars for Taiwan (“the rolling stock”) and has shipped them from Hitachi’s Kasado Works to Taiwan. The shipment consists of 1 trainset (12 cars), part of the 12 trainsets (144 cars) ordered in May 2023 by Taiwan High Speed Rail Corporation (“THSRC”) from the HTSC.

The rolling stock is based on the N700S, the latest Shinkansen model operated by Central Japan Railway Company, and has been designed to meet the operating environment and needs of THSRC. Each trainset is approximately 300 meters long and will operate commercially at a maximum speed of 300 km/h. The shape of the lead cars reduces resistance generated when entering tunnels, while the traction system, which combines silicon carbide (SiC) devices with a blower-less cooling system, has enabled the equipment to be made smaller and lighter and has reduced power consumption. In addition, the trains are equipped with a self-propelled battery system using Toshiba’s lithium-ion batteries “SCiB™” as a backup power source in the event of a power outage. The system can either move the trains at low speed to a safe location or keep onboard facilities such as lighting and restrooms operational.

The exterior features a predominantly white front-end design, combined with orange, THSRC’s corporate color symbolizing a bright future, and the black line used on the currently operating 700T. This design preserves continuity with the 700T while expressing the innovation and sense of speed of a new-generation high-speed train.

The interior partially retains the colors used in the 700T trainsets in the Standard Car seats, while the Business Car features a gray color scheme, creating a more subdued and refined atmosphere. Passenger comfort and convenience have been further enhanced through the adoption of reclining seats with a seat cushion that lowers as the seat reclines in the Standard Car, wraparound seats in the Business Car, a full-active suspension system that significantly reduces vibration, and power outlets at every seat.

GE Vernova, CG Power shares rebound from Friday's sell-off; Analysts advice whether you should buy
sum: Nomura has highlighted that Friday's move was an "overreaction" to what is a narrow exemption, and that the market participants read it as a competitive threat and sold these companies.
Shares of GE Vernova T&D Ltd., CG Power Ltd., Siemens Energy India Ltd., and Hitachi Energy India Ltd. are rebounding on Monday, July 6, after a sharp sell-off during Friday's trading session.

All the four companies highlighted above had declined between 7% to 9% after a memo from the Ministry of Finance, flagged by brokerages such as IIFL, had granted a two-year exemption to four Chinese companies to supply only from Indian manufacturing facilities, even as import restrictions still remain in place.

According to brokerage firm Jefferies, the demand-supply mismatch continues despite the local supply. It said that even as supply is growing between 80% to 90%, shortage and firm pricing is likely to continue going forward.
It highlighted Hitachi Energy & Siemens Energy as the top picks from this space and sees the recent correction as a buying opportunity.

Over financial year 2009-2020, the exempted players won 9% of the transmission-linked tenders by Power Grid, Nomura highlighted, adding that there is uneven capacity readiness across the four exempted entities as only one appears to be running near-optimal utilization.
"Two-year window is too short to underwrite meaningful capacity expansion in India," Nomura said, adding that GE Vernova T&D and CG Power are its top picks within this space.
